caption:
Your Ottawa itinerary starts here 🌷🇨🇦 
Did you know? Every year, over 1 million tulips are planted across Ottawa; a tradition dating back to 1953, born from the Netherlands gifting Canada tulip bulbs after WWII as a symbol of gratitude 🇳🇱🇨🇦 One of the most beautiful stories behind a festival, ever.  The Canadian Tulip Festival is in full swing, the weather is gorgeous and the long weekend is the perfect excuse to go. 
@ottawatourism @cdntulipfest   📌 Save this itinerary and start planning 
🌷 WHERE TO FIND TULIPS

📍 Commissioners Park & Dows Lake: the main hub and my favorite spot 
📍 Major’s Hill Park: tulips with Parliament Hill as your backdrop 
📍 Parliament Hill: iconic Canadian setting in full bloom
📍 ByWard Market Courtyard: blooms around every corner 
📍 Canadian Museum of History: stunning riverside views + tulips

☕ WHERE TO EAT

@parliament_cafe elevated coffee steps from Parliament Hill
@littlevictoriescoffee — Ottawa’s best specialty coffee roaster
@wilf_ada — cozy scratch diner, best brunch in the city 
@cantinagia — neighbourhood Italian, incredible homemade pasta 
@raphaelperuviancuisine — award-winning Peruvian cuisine
@starlingottawa — contemporary dishes in a stunning ByWard heritage building

🏨 WHERE TO STAY

@thelordelginhotel — classic Ottawa landmark steps from Parliament Hill

📍 SPOTS TO VISIT

✨ Ottawa Sign — the iconic illuminated letters at York Street Plaza in ByWard Market. Perfect photo stop, especially at night
🧺 Picnic at Major’s Hill — grab a bite from @botteganicastro
🕷️ Maman spider sculpture at National Gallery — 1 of 6 in the world
⛪ Notre Dame cathedral basilica — breathtaking Gothic cathedral
🌿 Kìwekì Point — best panoramic views in the city
🦕 Museum of Nature — dinosaurs, birds & a stunning heritage building
🏡 Rideau Hall — the Governor General’s stunning estate, open to the public

✨ THINGS TO DO

🚌 Hop on @graylineottawa double-decker bus
🚢 Rideau Canal cruise
🫖 Fairmont Château Laurier afternoon tea

caption:
Ever fed a deer from your car? 🥹🦌 Welcome to @parcomega 

📽️ @explore_with_naz
📍Parc Omega
🚗 1.5 hrs from Montreal & 1 hr from Ottawa

🎟️ Entry Fee:
▪️Adult 16 to 64: $46.09
▪️Senior 65+: $40.87
▪️Children 6 to 15: $33.91
▪️Children 2 to 5: $17.39

Parc Omega is a 12 km wildlife adventure where you can drive through breathtaking landscapes and see animals like wolves, elk, moose, bison, deer, and black bears in their natural habitat. The journey takes around 1.5 hours and is packed with unforgettable encounters!

❄️ Why visit in winter?
Winter at Parc Omega offers a peaceful, intimate experience with fewer crowds, magical snowy landscapes, and the chance to see animals in their stunning winter coats.

🏕️ Accommodations:
Want to stay overnight? The park offers rustic chalets, tipis, and log cabins for an immersive nature experience.

✨ Add Parc Omega to your winter bucket list & share it with your adventure buddies!

caption:
A château escape above the St. Lawrence River 🌊🏰✨

Staying at @fairmontmanoir felt like living inside a painting, perched between the mountains and the river, where every sunrise glows over Charlevoix and every sunset paints the cliffs in gold.

Our room overlooked the St. Lawrence, and mornings began with peaceful breakfasts and fall colors all around. 

Days were spent wandering the historic halls, relaxing at Moment Spa, playing golf and mini golf with breathtaking views, and swimming between the indoor and outdoor pools.

Evenings were a culinary journey; from elegant dining at Le Saint-Laurent, to cozy dinners at Le Bellerive and Bar La Brise, each meal a taste of Charlevoix’s charm.

Built over a century ago, this landmark blends old-world grandeur with the beauty of nature. A place where history, luxury, and tranquility meet.

caption:
Must-Visit in Fall near Montreal 🍁

Just 1.5 hours from Montreal, there’s a place where fiery autumn leaves frame a lakeside abbey, and silence feels almost magical. Welcome to Abbaye de Saint-Benoît-du-Lac.

📍 Abbaye de Saint-Benoît-du-Lac, Eastern Townships, Quebec, Canada
🎥 @explore_with_naz

🍂 What Makes It Special in Fall?
- The abbey is surrounded by hills that explode in red, orange, and gold foliage 
- Its unique architecture (granite & colorful brick) stands out against the vibrant forest
- You can wander the orchards and taste apple cider straight from the monks’ harvest 
- Join a guided tour to learn about the abbey’s history and unique design
- Go apple picking in their orchards (3,500+ trees) during the harvest season
- Inside, the peaceful atmosphere and Gregorian chants - create a calming, one-of-a-kind vibe

✨ Why You’ll Love Visiting:
- It’s not crowded, a real hidden gem compared to other fall spots
- Perfect blend of nature, history, food, and peace in one stop
- Amazing for photography: abbey towers + autumn trees + Lake Memphrémagog in the background = magic 

📖 Did you know?
- Built in 1912 by Benedictine monks, who still live and work here today
- Their orchards hold over 3,500 apple trees 
- The abbey is famous for its cheeses and ciders, made right on site
- You can actually attend daily chant services, a unique cultural experience.

caption:
Owl’s Head Hike - A Must-Do Fall Hike in Quebec 🍂✨ 

🎥 @explore_with_naz 

One of the most rewarding hikes near Montreal with stunning fall views over Lake Memphremagog ✨

Here’s what you need to know before going:

📍 Location: Owl’s Head Ski Lodge (40 chemin du Mont Owl’s Head, Mansonville, QC)

🚶 Trail Options:
- Panorama Trail: 3.3 km (one-way) – forest ascent 🌲
- Abénakis-Maçonnique Trail: 2.3 km (one-way) – historic + steep climb
- Loops: Go up one trail, descend the other or ski trails

⚖️ Difficulty: Moderate to Difficult (final climb is steep!)

⛰ Elevation Gain: ~520 m

📏 Distance: ~6–6.5 km round-trip (depending on loop)

⏱ Duration: ~2 hrs (round trip)

🐶 Dog Friendly: Yes, leashed dogs allowed 

🔥 No Camping/Fires: Strictly prohibited

🚗 From Montreal: ~1h30 drive

🍂 Best Time for Fall Colors: Late Sept – Mid Oct

🚡 Chairlift Option: Don’t feel like hiking? Take the Summit Chairlift (around $22 per person) for a faster ride up + views all the way!

✨ At the top: panoramic views of Lake Memphremagog + surrounding mountains like Jay Peak & Orford 🌄

caption:
Quebec City, a Christmas postcard brought to life 🎄✨

📌 Things to Know Before Planning your Quebec City Trip:

🎄 Christmas Decorations
The city is fully decorated from November 20 to mid-January; the most magical time of the year!

❄️ How Cold Is Quebec City?
Be ready for true Canadian winter temps. Pack layers, winter boots, and hand warmers!
• November: ~ 0°C to -5°C
• December: ~ -5°C to -15°C
• January: ~ -10°C to -20°C

🥨 German Christmas Market
Runs from November 20 to December 23; a must-see for food, crafts, and cozy holiday vibes.

🎅 December 24 & 25
• Dec 24: everything is open, most shops close at 5 PM
• Dec 25: some cafés & restaurants in Old Quebec open, but shops stay closed

🌨️ For a Snowy Christmas
If you’re dreaming of snow, check AccuWeather — it often snows a few days before Christmas.

✨ Best Time to Avoid Crowd
• Late November is less busy, but still beautifully decorated!
• Early morning (7 am) is the best time to capture beautiful postcards pictures.

🏰 Hôtel de Glace
If you plan to visit the Ice Hotel, it opens on January 4th.

📍 Must-Visit Places in Quebec City
• Old Quebec (Vieux-Québec)
• Petit-Champlain
• Château Frontenac
• Place Royale
• Dufferin Terrace
• The German Christmas Market
• Parliament Hill & the Grande Allée lights
• Montmorency Falls 
• Strom Spa

Quebec City truly feels like stepping into a Christmas movie; these tips will help you make the most of your trip 🎄❄️❤️

caption:
The Dreamiest Fall Hikes in Québec 🍂💛

Tucked away in Charlevoix, just 1 hour from Québec City (and 4 hours from Montréal), Mont du Dôme in Zec des Martres is a must-add to your bucket list for next fall. ✨

The trail winds through golden forests, opens up to mountain view, glowing with colour, and even surprises you with a peaceful lake along the way. 🩵

It’s calm, scenic, and one of those spots that perfectly captures the beauty of Québec in autumn.

✨ Trail info:
📍 Location: Mont du Dome, Charlevoix
🥾 Distance: 8 km loop
⛰️ Elevation gain: ~ 467 m
⏱️ Duration: 3.5 – 4 hours
🔥 Difficulty: Difficult 
🐶 Dogs allowed on leash
🚗 1 h from Québec City | 4 h from Montréal
⏳ Best time to visit in fall: Last week of September to First week of October 

PS: The photos were taken on October 6th — save this one for next fall! 🍁

You can find this hike on @alltrails — super helpful since there are three different summits on the route! 🗺️ If you only want to reach this specific one, keep the app open to stay on track. The trail is well-marked with clear signs too, so it’s easy to follow.

caption:
You don’t want to miss this hike this fall 🍂

🍁 Follow for more fall discoveries! @explore_with_naz 

The Mont King trail at Parc régional Val-David is a total dream in autumn. Perfect view, crisp air & golden leaves. 

📍 Location:
Parc régional Val-David–Val-Morin, Laurentides, Québec — Mont King trail 

📆 Best time in fall:
Peak colours usually late-September through mid-October. 

💪 Difficulty:
Moderate — enough climb to get your heart pumping and earn the view, but still family-friendly if you’re used to trails.

⏱ Duration / Distance:
About 6.9 km / ~2-2½ hours round-trip for Mont King. The “big Mont King loop” is ~6.7 km, ~3 hours.

🚗 Distance from Montreal:
≈ 1-1.5 hours drive (depending on traffic) to Val-David.

🐾 Dog-friendly:
Leashed dogs are welcome — perfect for an autumn adventure with your pup!

🔥 Pro tip: Go at sunrise — golden hour lighting, serene vibes, and you’ll probably have the summit mostly to yourself. Bring layers because mornings can be chilly.

caption:
✨ A Fairytale Stay at Canada’s Castle on the Coast ✨
🏰 @fairmontempress 

Nestled in the heart of Victoria, BC, the Fairmont Empress stands as a testament to timeless elegance and modern luxury. From the moment we arrived, it felt like stepping into a royal escape right on the harbor.

Victoria in spring is pure magic — the hotel was surrounded by blooming tulips, and the view of the sparkling Inner Harbour was just breathtaking.

One of the highlights? Staying on Fairmont Gold, their exclusive ‘hotel within a hotel’ experience. We were spoiled with access to a private lounge offering delicious breakfasts, afternoon tea snacks, and sunset canapés — all with panoramic views of the harbor and Parliament. Golden hour from that lounge is something I’ll never forget. 💫

We also enjoyed a beautiful breakfast in bed, relaxed with their signature afternoon tea (a must-do in Victoria!), and had an incredible dinner at Q at the Empress — such a chic space with amazing local flavours.

💫Fun fact: The Empress has been welcoming guests since 1908 and has hosted everyone from royalty to celebrities. It’s now a Forbes recommended + MICHELIN Key hotel, and trust me, it lives up to every bit of the hype.

If you’re planning a trip to Vancouver Island, make sure this iconic gem is on your list 🤍

caption:
10 Things to Do in Victoria, BC 🇨🇦

Save this for your Victoria trip! 😇🙌🏻

🎥 @explore_with_naz 

Victoria is the perfect mix of charm, nature, and history. From ocean views and lush gardens to hidden alleys and iconic landmarks, this coastal city has something for everyone. 

Here are 10 unforgettable things to do:

1️⃣ Fly in by Sea Plane @harbourair ✈️
We booked this tour through @getyourguide — this was the most scenic way to arrive in Victoria. A smooth, quick flight with breathtaking views. @getyourguidecommunity 

2️⃣ Walk Along Victoria Harbour ⛴️
Take a relaxing stroll along the lively waterfront lined with shops, street performers, and views of float planes.

3️⃣ Visit or stay at the @fairmontempress 🏰
This historic hotel is a Victoria icon—perfect for photos and soaking in Edwardian charm. 

4️⃣ Tour the Parliament Buildings 🏛️
Take a free guided tour or explore the beautiful architecture of British Columbia’s legislative buildings.

5️⃣ Explore Butchart Gardens 🌷
A must-visit, this world-famous garden features over 900 varieties of plants across stunning themed sections. @thebutchartgardens 

6️⃣ Enjoy Afternoon Tea at the Fairmont Empress☕️
Treat yourself to an elegant high tea experience in a royal-like setting. @fairmontempress 

7️⃣ Wander Through Chinatown & Fan Tan Alley 🐲
Canada’s oldest Chinatown is home to the narrowest street in North America! 

8️⃣ Relax in Beacon Hill Park 🦚
A peaceful park with lakes, gardens, and even roaming peacocks—great for a laid-back afternoon. 

9️⃣ Eat at Fisherman’s Wharf ⚓️
Grab fresh seafood and explore the colorful floating homes at this fun and casual harbor spot. @fishermanswharf 

🔟 Go Whale Watching 🐋
Victoria is one of the best places in Canada to see orcas and humpbacks—book a tour for an unforgettable adventure. @princeofwhaleswhalewatching

Free under 6

- No hiking required—fully accessible to strollers & wheelchairs

caption:
Memories from Our Magical Trip to Mont-Tremblant ⛷️❄️❤️

Invited by @tourismemonttremblant ✨

Mont-Tremblant in winter is pure magic! From snow-covered mountains to cozy village vibes, this trip was truly unforgettable. 

Here’s everything we did on our trip!
Day 1: 
🏨 Stayed at @marriottbonvoy – Waking up to snowy mountain views was a dream! The cozy rooms, relaxing outdoor hot baths, and perfect location made our stay extra special.
🚡 Rode the Free Gondola with @monttremblant – Taking in the breathtaking views from above was an absolute highlight!
🏡 Explored the Charming Pedestrian Village – Strolling through the village felt like stepping into a winter postcard! Twinkling lights, festive decorations, concerts, and boutique shops made it such a magical experience. 
🍩 Tried a Classic Treat at @beavertails – Nothing beats a warm, crispy BeaverTail on a chilly day—our favorite winter indulgence!
🍕 Had the Best Italian Pizza at @a_mano_trattoria – Fresh ingredients, wood-fired perfection, and cozy vibes—this spot is a must for pizza lovers.

Day 2: 
🛷 Went Dog Sledding with @tremblantactivities – This was hands down one of the most exciting things we’ve ever done! Racing through snowy trails with the most energetic huskies was an experience we’ll never forget.
❄️ Snow Tubing at @aventures.neige – We felt like kids again speeding down the hills—so much fun and non-stop laughs!
🥃 Après-Ski Cocktails at @fairmonttremblant – The perfect way to warm up after a day in the snow! Highly recommend their signature hot toddy.
🎵 Ended the Night with Live Music at @ville_monttremblant @mparthur_ – The energy, the atmosphere, and the music made for the perfect ending to an amazing day.

We had such an incredible time exploring Tremblant, and we can’t wait to go back!

caption:
Votre week-end de rêve vous attend dans Charlevoix! 🦉✨

📸 @explore_with_naz 

Que vous recherchiez la détente, l’aventure ou un mélange des deux, cet endroit a tout pour plaire! 
Notre séjour au @chaletlajoliechouette n’a été rien de moins que magique! Niché au cœur de Charlevoix, ce chalet luxueux et moderne était l’évasion parfaite vers la beauté de la nature avec nos amis. 

📍Chalet La Jolie Chouette (CITQ: 315265)

Voici pourquoi nous l’avons adoré:

🌄 Vues époustouflantes: perché sur une montagne privée avec vue panoramique sur le fleuve Saint-Laurent et la Baie Saint-Paul, le paysage est à couper le souffle à chaque tournant.

🏡 Confort spacieux et moderne: construit en 2023, le chalet s’étend sur 4500 pi² avec des fenêtres du sol au plafond, alliant luxe moderne et chaleur douillette, parfait pour les groupes ou les familles jusqu’à 16 personnes.

🔥 Espaces de détente: Nous avons passé des soirées douillettes près du foyer au gaz, nous nous sommes détendus dans le spa extérieur et nous nous sommes réunis autour du foyer sous les étoiles.

🎮 Divertissement pour tous: Trois salons, une piscine à débordement, un baby-foot, une aire de jeux pour enfants et deux terrasses (dont une installation pour barbecue) ont permis à chacun de profiter facilement de ses activités préférées.

🏞️ Emplacement: À seulement 5 minutes en voiture de la charmante ville de Baie St-Paul, où vous pourrez découvrir des galeries d’art, la cuisine locale, des festivals et plus encore.

❄️ Aventure toute l’année: Des sentiers de motoneige juste devant la porte au ski à proximité, en passant par la randonnée et même les excursions d’observation des baleines, ce chalet est le point de départ idéal pour explorer Charlevoix!

Que vous recherchiez une retraite paisible ou une aventure de groupe passionnante, le Chalet La Jolie Chouette offre le meilleur des deux mondes. J’ai hâte d’y retourner! 💫

caption:
Ever fed a deer from your car? 🥹🦌 Welcome to @parcomega 

📽️ @explore_with_naz
📍Parc Omega
🚗 1.5 hrs from Montreal & 1 hr from Ottawa

🎟️ Entry Fee:
▪️Adult 16 to 64: $46.09
▪️Senior 65+: $40.87
▪️Children 6 to 15: $33.91
▪️Children 2 to 5: $17.39

Parc Omega is a 12 km wildlife adventure where you can drive through breathtaking landscapes and see animals like wolves, elk, moose, bison, deer, and black bears in their natural habitat. The journey takes around 1.5 hours and is packed with unforgettable encounters!

❄️ Why visit in winter?
Winter at Parc Omega offers a peaceful, intimate experience with fewer crowds, magical snowy landscapes, and the chance to see animals in their stunning winter coats.

🏕️ Accommodations:
Want to stay overnight? The park offers rustic chalets, tipis, and log cabins for an immersive nature experience.

✨ Add Parc Omega to your winter bucket list & share it with your adventure buddies!

5️⃣ Bromont
📍 1.5 hours from Montreal

🔺 Explore the old town’s boutiques and restaurants.

caption:
Crisp air & golden leaves: Fall in Parc national de la Jacques-Cartier! 🍂 

🎥 @explore_with_naz ; recorded on October 2nd

📍 30 mins from Quebec City, and 3.5 hrs from Montreal; this park is a must-see in the fall!

📆 Best time to visit: Late September to mid-October for the vibrant colors.

💰 Entrance Fee: $9.25 per person.

🥾 Popular Trails: 

Easy Trails:
🔸La Rivière-Sautauriski (4.8 km, 1.5 h): Accessible for strollers with big wheels, this trail offers scenic views of the river. Dog-friendly.
🔸 L'Aperçu (2.2 km, 45 min): A quick loop along Belleau brook, perfect for discovery. Dog-friendly.
🔸Le Confluent (1.7 km, 35 min): A short loop around a diverse delta of terrestrial and aquatic habitats.

Intermediate Trails:
🔹Le Draveur Sud (14.8 km, 5 h): Forested trail with a refreshing stop by the Jacques-Cartier River.
🔹 La Croisée (15.8 km, 4.5 h): A longer trail with stunning views of the Jacques-Cartier River and steep valley walls.
🔹L'Éperon (5.4 km, 2 h): Hike along the river with breathtaking valley views. Dog-friendly.
🔹 Les Coulées (10.4 km, 3.5 h): Crisscross the Belleau valley with moderate elevation gain. Dog-friendly.

Difficult Trails:
▪️Les Loups (5 km, 2 h to the first belvedere; 11 km, 3.5 h to the second belvedere): Stunning panoramic views of the valley from one of the park’s highest points.
▪️Le Scotora (16 km, 5.25 h): A long hike to Mont Adante with spectacular views of valley gorges.
▪️L'Escarpement (11.2 km, 4 h): A steady rise through the forest leading to an exceptional lookout from 350 meters.

❗️Drone usage is not allowed in the park. We took one shot at the entrance; then we asked and got informed that it’s not permitted.
